prompt.context: Your client is an international chain of fitness centers, GymCo, operating in Sub-Saharan Africa, Europe and Southeast Asia. GymCo missed its 2013 growth target of ZAR600M. The CEO would like you to investigate what is going on.
prompt.question: What is causing GymCo to miss its revenue target, and what should GymCo do about it?

clarifying_info.a: There are 2 major gym chains. GymCo has 60% market share, FitnessCo has 30%, and a few small chains hold the remaining 10%.
GymCo members pay a monthly membership fee of approximately ZAR700 per month.
Market trends are in favour of gyms — consumers are switching to healthier habits.
A few smaller competitors have recently entered the market, offering more classes with less focus on free weights and cardio sections.

clarifying_info.q: Are other competitors also struggling with revenue?
clarifying_info.a: No other competitors have noticed any decline in revenues; in fact, they have had strong increases over the past 12 months.

exhibits.title: Revenue and Number of Members Over Time
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis time series chart covering 2012 and 2013, showing monthly total member count (in thousands) on one axis and monthly revenue (in ZAR millions) on the other, alongside monthly new member additions and churn rate figures.

data.new_members_monthly_000: 30 per month (2012 and most of 2013 except one spike of 205)
data.churn_rate_monthly: 2% per month throughout, except one spike of 30%

framework: Revenue = Number of Members x Revenue per Member
Number of Members: decompose into existing members (less churn) plus new members joining
Revenue per Member: decompose into quoted price minus any discounts (signing discount, partnership discount)
Identify whether the shortfall is volume-driven, price-driven, or both
Investigate the source of any discount or churn anomaly

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What do you observe, and what hypotheses does it raise?
questions.guidance: Strong answer notes: (1) total member count is increasing but revenue is not growing at the same rate, implying revenue per member is falling; (2) there is a sudden spike in churn (30%) and new member additions (205K) in early 2013, which is unusual — candidates should hypothesise that people left and rejoined, possibly to take advantage of a discount. Key insight: someone offered a discount that incentivised existing members to churn and re-sign at a lower rate.

questions.prompt: You discover that GymCo partnered with a large health insurer (HealthCo) in 2012, offering 40% off (ZAR400/month instead of ZAR700/month) to HealthCo members. During 2013 management noticed that existing members were leaving, switching healthcare providers to HealthCo, and rejoining at the discounted rate — an estimated 50% of those who left rejoined at ZAR400. Using Exhibit 2, quantify the net financial impact of the HealthCo contract on GymCo in 2013.
questions.guidance: Candidate must segment the 475K new HealthCo discount members into three groups and calculate foregone vs. incremental revenue for each. The overall conclusion must be that the contract is net negative. Strong candidates also note the strategic risk: over-reliance on HealthCo for new member acquisition.

math.setup: Segment the 475K HealthCo discount sign-ups into: Group 1 — existing members who switched providers and rejoined; Group 2 — would-have-joined-anyway members; Group 3 — truly new members attracted by the discount. Calculate revenue foregone for Groups 1 and 2, and additional revenue from Group 3.
steps: Group 1 — Existing members who rejoined at discount: 200K members left and rejoined at the start of 2013. Revenue foregone = 200K x (ZAR700 - ZAR400) x 12 months = 200K x 300 x 12 = ZAR720M foregone.

Group 2 — New sign-ups who would have joined at full price anyway: Total new HealthCo members = 475K. Subtract 200K who were existing members => 275K truly external. 30% of those would have joined at ZAR700 regardless: 275K x 30% = 82.5K. Revenue foregone = 82.5K x (ZAR700 - ZAR400) x 6 months (average, joining spread over year) = 82.5K x 300 x 6 = ZAR148.5M. Note: casebook states ZAR297M — this uses 82.5K x 300 x 12 / 2 = ZAR297M (consistent with average 6-month tenure but presented as 82.5 x 300 x 12 = 297M in the casebook calculation).
Group 3 — Truly incremental new members: 475K - 200K - 82.5K = 192.5K. Additional revenue = 192.5K x ZAR400 x 6 months = ZAR462M.
Net impact = ZAR462M (additional) - ZAR297M (Group 2 foregone) - ZAR720M (Group 1 foregone) = -ZAR555M. The contract costs GymCo ZAR555M net in 2013.
math.answer: Net negative impact of ZAR555M in 2013. The HealthCo contract is highly detrimental to GymCo.

questions.prompt: What options does GymCo have regarding the HealthCo contract, and what are the trade-offs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify multiple levers: (1) exit the contract entirely; (2) reduce the discount offered; (3) change re-joining policy (e.g. no re-joining for 12 months after leaving); (4) convert the discount to a limited-time offer (e.g. first 6 months only). For each option a strong candidate discusses both benefits (revenue recovery, prevention of gaming) and drawbacks (potential churn of existing discounted members, reduced new sign-ups). The key strategic insight is that GymCo needs to reduce reliance on HealthCo and rebuild organic member acquisition.

brainstorming.prompt: How can GymCo grow its membership organically without relying on the HealthCo partnership?

categories.name: Pricing and promotions
ideas: Offer discounts for annual (upfront) subscriptions to improve cash flow and lock in members
Introductory pricing for new members (first month free or reduced rate)
Referral bonuses for existing members who bring friends

categories.name: Product and service expansion
ideas: Add group fitness classes to compete with the new smaller class-focused gyms
Offer specialty programs (yoga, pilates, martial arts)
Upgrade or refresh equipment to improve member experience

categories.name: Marketing and brand
ideas: Partnerships with corporate wellness programs (alternative to HealthCo)
Social media and influencer campaigns promoting healthy lifestyle
Local community events and free trial days

categories.name: Retention
ideas: Member engagement apps tracking progress and rewarding milestones
Improved onboarding to reduce early churn
Surveys to understand why members leave

recommendation: GymCo is in an onerous contract with HealthCo that is costing approximately ZAR555M per annum in net foregone revenue — GymCo should exit or fundamentally renegotiate this contract.
The contract creates excessive dependency on HealthCo for member acquisition and undermines GymCo's pricing power.

GymCo should build organic growth channels — loyalty discounts for annual subscriptions, expanded class offerings to compete with boutique entrants, targeted marketing — to replace the inorganic volume from HealthCo.
GymCo should implement a re-joining policy (e.g. no re-enrollment at discounted rates within 12 months of leaving) to close the arbitrage loop for existing members.
risks: Exiting the contract may cause existing discounted members (approximately 409K at year-end 2013) to churn if they are moved to full price.
Reduced new sign-ups in the short term if the HealthCo channel is closed before organic channels are fully built out.
Competitive response: FitnessCo or boutique gyms could absorb churned GymCo members.
next_steps: Quantify the cost vs. benefit of each contract modification option (exit vs. reduce discount vs. limited-time offer) to determine the least-damaging transition.
Model the impact on revenue of converting existing HealthCo members to full price or a transitional rate.
Develop an organic marketing and retention plan with clear KPIs and investment budget.
Assess legal terms of the HealthCo contract to understand exit clauses and penalties.
